text: Yes, the sources agree on tree-cover loss in 2012 on this property. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset directly observed a 1.4-hectare loss in 2012 (0.04% of the asset). The JRC 2020 reference confirms 51% of that area was still forest in 2020, meeting the corroboration rule. The Uruguayan MGAP map further details that the loss occurred in planted forests (not native forest). All three datasets are spatially and temporally aligned, with no conflicts. The evidence meets the project’s corroboration criteria.
